description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/chat.rs:108-136, particularly the comment at line 117 ('O(1) fetch instead of O(n) per-create fetches').

The hoisted fetch at line 123-126 reads every Chat in the account (no filter pushdown):
    backend.get_objects::<Chat>(caller, &account_id, None, None)

For an account with K Direct chats already + N to-create in this batch:
- Old (per-create) cost: O(N * K) reads.
- New (hoisted) cost: O(K + N) reads — one big fetch + a HashSet contains check per create.

This IS an improvement, but the comment claims 'O(1) fetch' which is wrong. The cost of the fetch is O(K) in the existing chat count; for an account with 100,000 chats and a batch of 5 creates, every batch pays a 100K-record scan.

Worse: each cycle of the test suite (and each production /set call) repeats the full scan. With ALL chat types fetched (Direct + Group + Channel + any future kinds), the filter at line 127-131 only retains Direct chats, wasting cycles on the rest.

Mitigations:
1. Add a backend.find_direct_chats_by_contact(caller, account_id, contact_ids) -> HashMap<Id, Id> method that the backend can push down to a real index (SQL: WHERE kind='direct' AND contact_id IN (...)) returning only the relevant rows.
2. Or: skip the hoist when create batch is small and a single chat fetch by contact_id would be cheaper (the per-create fetch's actual cost is O(K) in MemoryBackend too — there's no point-lookup index — so the trade-off isn't obvious in the test backend, but is in production).

This is a 'comment is wrong' more than 'code is slow' bug at the kit level; the kit's choice not to expose a typed query is the real cost driver, tracked by JMAP-63k.9 per the comment chain.
title: Chat/set create's 'O(1) fetch' is actually O(N total chats in account); comment misleading
